property_summary: For any admissible caller, a play with the exact ticket price must change the pot by a multiple of TICKET_AMOUNT (pot % 10 == 0 after the call, whether the round is won or lost); the mutant adds a constant 1 instead, leaving pot % 10 == 1 and breaking the rule.

For any seed-driven sequence of valid 10-wei plays, play() must never revert: the winner's payout equals the currently funded pot, which the reference keeps in sync by resetting pot to 0 after each win, whereas the mutant lets pot grow beyond the contract's balance so a later win reverts on transfer.

For any successful play, the recorded pot can never exceed the contract's actual ether balance (reference resets pot to 0 on a win, keeping pot <= balance always), whereas the mutant leaves the stale pot in place after paying it out, making pot() > address(c).balance after any winning play.

For any successful play, if the player wins (their balance increases by the payout), the pot must be reset to zero; the reference always does this, while the mutant leaves the pot at its post-accumulation value (10) after a win.

For any winning play (and any preceding history), the winner's ether balance after the play is exactly their stake plus TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE (9 wei), because the reference resets pot to 0 after every win; the mutant lets pot accumulate so a second winner is overpaid (pot - FEE includes the stale pot) and their balance is 10 wei higher.

For every caller and every (timestamp, difficulty) pair, a play wins exactly when keccak256(timestamp, difficulty, sender) is even (pot resets to 0 and the bank receives the fee); the mutant inverts this, so on odd-parity inputs the reference leaves pot at TICKET_AMOUNT while the mutant resets it (and vice versa).
After two non-winning ticket purchases of 10 wei each, the pot must hold 20 (accumulation), otherwise 0 if a win occurred in between; the mutant resets it to 10 and breaks this.
